raw_request: Create the dsh-memory plugin. Start with project planning and governance, summarize the design, and produce a high-level design for approval before detailed design.
understood_objective: Design a DSH-native memory plugin where tool-call and compaction-summary outputs carry a mandatory index-ready memory field, entries accumulate in a pending index, and only a successful automatic or manual memory compaction commits raw entries plus an organized delta into versioned long-term knowledge.
acceptance_criteria: DSH remains the runtime and the first implementation does not fork DSH core.
Session journal truth, model-visible surface, working state, knowledge truth, index projection, and control state have explicit owners and boundaries.
Knowledge updates append revisions with evidence; prior revisions remain queryable and reversible.
Model-visible memory index changes only at session creation or successful compaction; ordinary memory writes do not mutate the stable request prefix.
Unresolved failures stay model-visible until their result and lesson are absorbed; source events remain immutable.
Models may propose memory candidates but deterministic host rules own admission, conflict handling, and final persistence.
Compaction, index promotion, crash recovery, and DSH surface replacement have one verified consistency protocol.
Cache, recall, evidence lineage, correctness, and recovery behavior have positive and negative verification gates.
Every eligible tool-call output and compaction-summary output contains a schema-versioned memory field; an empty array is explicit when nothing is worth remembering.
Tool-call memory may describe only completed events before the current tool execution; the current unobserved tool result cannot be recorded as success.
Validated memory emissions append directly to a durable pending index but do not enter long-term knowledge before a successful compaction boundary.

When the index reaches its configured limit, the compaction owner selects the oldest ten percent deterministically and replaces their active index projection with lossless child-referenced compressed segments.
Every compaction persists both immutable raw index entries and a validated organization delta, then promotes one categorized index epoch without deleting earlier raw entries or organization epochs.
A memory-organize command supports incremental and full modes through the same compaction transaction owner.
Implementation occurs only in clean independent worktrees; root main remains an inspection and integration surface.
The delivery order is high-level design, architecture zones, individually verified foundation capabilities, foundation module, DSH plugin, and profile wiring.
No foundation capability enters the foundation module until its contract, positive and negative tests, public-API blackbox, recovery behavior, and architecture boundary evidence pass.
non_goals: Shipping a management UI in the first milestone.
Writing pending emissions directly into the long-term knowledge store outside a successful compaction boundary.
Copying Cairn or AppSDK implementation into this project.
Using embeddings or a search subagent for every recall request.
assumptions: The prior design is an input hypothesis; DSH and Cairn source seams, versions, licenses, and runtime behavior must be re-pinned before detailed design.
PromptContext, Session Surface, CompactionEngine, Cordis services, and fresh subagents remain the intended DSH integration seams.
V1 targets one local plugin store and one DSH profile before broader deployment.
ambiguities: Exact DSH commit and public APIs to pin.
Whether BasicCompactionEngine subclassing can provide the required ordering without replacing the full provider.
Exact reusable Cairn components and license obligations.
V1 deployment entrypoint and blackbox environment.
Exact DSH response-protocol seam that can carry the mandatory memory field beside tool calls without modifying provider payload semantics.
Exact Node-to-Rust bridge packaging supported by the pinned DSH build and distribution path.

questions.question: Approve the high-level design and governance baseline before detailed design and source implementation.
